summary: South Africa beat New Zealand 12-11 in the Rugby World Cup final at the Stade de France to win a record fourth title, in a wet, controversial match full of cards and officiating debate. The All Blacks played most of the game a man down after captain Sam Cane's red card but lost by a point after Richie Mo'unga missed a conversion. The result also marked farewells for coaches Jacques Nienaber and Ian Foster and several veteran players.
one_line: The Springboks edged the All Blacks 12-11 in a card-filled Rugby World Cup final in Paris to win a record fourth title.
key_facts: South Africa beat New Zealand 12-11 in the Rugby World Cup final at the Stade de France, with 80,065 fans in attendance and rain falling.
The win gave the Springboks a record fourth World Cup, moving them past the All Blacks; it was their third one-point knockout victory in a row.
Sam Cane, the All Blacks captain, had a yellow card for a high shot on Jesse Kriel upgraded to red and watched 53 minutes from the sidelines.
Siya Kolisi was shown a yellow card for a high shot on Ardie Savea but returned; Cheslin Kolbe was yellow-carded in the 73rd minute for a deliberate knockdown.
Beauden Barrett scored the match's only try in the 58th minute, but Richie Mo'unga's missed conversion proved the difference.
Handre Pollard kicked four three-pointers to lead the Springboks' scoring.
Pieter-Steph du Toit, the 2019 World Rugby player of the year, made 28 tackles in his best match in four years.
Shannon Frizell was yellow-carded early for an illegal cleanout on hooker Bongi Mbonambi, who was replaced by Deon Fourie in the third minute.
Wayne Barnes refereed the final and was booed relentlessly; in the 80th minute the Springboks won a scrum reset and held onto the ball.
Rassie Erasmus is set to follow head coach Jacques Nienaber out, and Duane Vermeulen will retire; Nienaber and Erasmus are described as the greatest coaching duo in rugby history.
Ian Foster's tenure as All Blacks coach ended, with Scott Robertson to take over; Dane Coles, Sam Whitelock, Brodie Retallick and Aaron Smith are to end their international careers.
The Springboks led 12-3 after 34 minutes and 12-6 after 37 minutes before the All Blacks' late try left them one point behind.
The win echoed South Africa's 1995 victory at Ellis Park, where Nelson Mandela handed the William Webb Ellis Cup to Francois Pienaar, 28 years earlier.
